import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    target = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()

    # Determine watermark timestamp
    if len(watermark) == 0:
        high_ts = pd.Timestamp.min
    else:
        high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]

    # Step 1: keep only events strictly after the watermark
    filtered = cdc[cdc["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()

    # Step 2: per product_id, pick the latest event by (event_ts, event_seq)
    if len(filtered) > 0:
        filtered = filtered.sort_values(["product_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"])
        latest = filtered.groupby("product_id", as_index=False).tail(1)
    else:
        latest = filtered

    # Build snapshot indexed by product_id for easy upsert/delete
    snap = target.set_index("product_id")

    for row in latest.itertuples(index=False):
        pid = row.product_id
        if row.op == "D":
            if pid in snap.index:
                snap = snap.drop(index=pid)
        else:
            # Upsert (I or U)
            snap.loc[pid, "name"] = row.name
            snap.loc[pid, "price"] = row.price
            snap.loc[pid, "last_event_ts"] = row.event_ts

    result = snap.reset_index()

    # Enforce column order and dtypes matching target_snapshot schema
    result = result[["product_id", "name", "price", "last_event_ts"]]
    result["product_id"] = result["product_id"].astype("int64")
    result["price"] = result["price"].astype("float64")
    result["last_event_ts"] = pd.to_datetime(result["last_event_ts"]).astype("datetime64[us]")
    result["name"] = result["name"].astype(object)

    return {"new_snapshot": result}
